Signs of the World

Radioactive material

History

Mechanical engineer Cyrill Orly designed the radiation symbol in 1946 at the University of California, Berkeley Radiation Laboratory. The first signs showed it in magenta on blue, a shade chosen because it was expensive and unlikely to appear anywhere else. It was documented as an international symbol in 1963 and became the ISO 361 standard in 1974.

Adoption

The three-bladed symbol warns of radiation around the world, usually in black on yellow, while the United States also uses magenta. In 2007, a second sign with a skull and a running figure was added for dangerous radiation sources.
